hard_vocabulary.definition: Lasting for a very short time; transitory
hard_vocabulary.example: The ephemeral beauty of cherry blossoms makes them even more precious.
Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern society.

hard_vocabulary.definition: Having a ready insight into and understanding of things; mentally sharp or discerning
hard_vocabulary.example: Her perspicacious analysis of the situation helped us avoid a major crisis.

hard_vocabulary.definition: To make obscure, unclear, or unintelligible; to bewilder or confuse
hard_vocabulary.example: The politician tried to obfuscate the issue with complex jargon.

hard_vocabulary.definition: Generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival or less powerful person
hard_vocabulary.example: Despite winning the debate, she was magnanimous toward her opponent.

hard_vocabulary.definition: To use ambiguous language so as to conceal the truth or avoid committing oneself
hard_vocabulary.example: When asked about his plans, he equivocated rather than giving a direct answer.

hard_vocabulary.definition: A person who acts obsequiously toward someone important in order to gain advantage
hard_vocabulary.example: He was surrounded by sycophants who agreed with everything he said.

hard_vocabulary.definition: Reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little
hard_vocabulary.example: The taciturn scientist rarely spoke at meetings but his work spoke volumes.

hard_vocabulary.definition: To make something bad or unsatisfactory better; to improve
hard_vocabulary.example: The new policies were designed to ameliorate living conditions in the city.

hard_vocabulary.definition: Having an obstinately uncooperative attitude toward authority or discipline
hard_vocabulary.example: The recalcitrant student refused to follow the classroom rules.

hard_vocabulary.definition: To place or deal with close together for contrasting effect
hard_vocabulary.example: The artist juxtaposed light and dark colors to create a dramatic effect.

hard_vocabulary.definition: Carried out with a minimum of effort or reflection; done merely as a routine
hard_vocabulary.example: He gave a perfunctory nod before returning to his work.

hard_vocabulary.definition: Having or showing great knowledge or learning
hard_vocabulary.example: The erudite professor could discuss any topic with impressive depth.

hard_vocabulary.definition: Experienced in the imagination through the feelings or actions of another person
hard_vocabulary.example: She got vicarious pleasure from reading about others' adventures.

hard_vocabulary.definition: Not self-indulgent, especially when eating and drinking; moderate
hard_vocabulary.example: His abstemious lifestyle contributed to his longevity and good health.
